result.stdout:
rask — the Rask framework command-line tool

Usage: rask <command> [options]

Commands:
  new          Create a new Rask project from a template.
  dev          Run the app with hot reload (dotnet watch).
  generate     Scaffold a page, component, CRUD feature, background job, email, or cache into the current project.
  db           Manage EF Core migrations (add, remove, list, update, drop).
  deploy       Build and deploy the app to a single host over SSH (auto-HTTPS with --domain).
  info         Show Rask CLI, .NET SDK, and OS environment information.
  completion   Print a shell completion script (bash, zsh, or fish).

Run 'rask <command> --help' for command-specific usage.

Options:
  --version    Show the tool version.
  --help       Show help for a command.

Create a new Rask project from a template.

Usage: rask new <name> [--template server|wasm|wasm-hosted|native] [--auth] [--pwa] [--cqrs] [--data] [--jobs] [--mail] [--cache] [--outbox] [--push] [--snapshots] [--all-batteries] [--docker] [--host local|server] [--output <dir>]

Arguments:
  <name>   Name of the project to create (scaffolds ./<name>/).

Options:
  -t, --template <name>       Template to scaffold: server (default), wasm, wasm-hosted, or native.
  -o, --output <dir>          Directory to create the project in (default: ./<name>).
  -n, --name <name>           Project name, if not given positionally.
      --host <local|server>   Native host mode: local (default) or server. Native template only.
      --auth                  Add cookie authentication (login + members pages).
      --pwa                   Add a PWA manifest, icon, and offline page.
      --cqrs                  Wire up Rask.Cqrs (server template only).
      --data                  Pre-wire SQLite + EF Core: an AppDbContext ready for `rask generate feature --context AppDbContext` (server only).
      --docker                Add a Dockerfile and .dockerignore for container deploys.
      --no-restore            Don't run dotnet restore after scaffolding (for offline use).
      --force                 Scaffold into a directory that already has files in it, overwriting on collision.
      --jobs                  Durable background jobs on the app's own database (implies --data).

      --push                  Server-sent Web Push with subscribe endpoints (implies --pwa).
      --snapshots             Scheduled point-in-time SQLite backups (implies --data).

result.stdout:
Run the app with hot reload (dotnet watch).

Usage: rask dev [--project <path>] [--no-hot-reload] [-- <args passed to the app>]

Options:
  -p, --project <path>   Project to run (default: the project in the current directory).
      --no-hot-reload    Use a plain 'dotnet run' instead of 'dotnet watch' (no hot reload).

Examples:
  rask dev
  rask dev --project src/App
  rask dev -- --urls http://localhost:5000

Scaffold a page, component, CRUD feature, background job, email, or cache into the current project.

Usage: rask generate <page|component|feature|job|email|cache> <Name> [<field:type> ...] [options]

Arguments:
  <page|component|feature|job|email|cache>   What to scaffold (aliases: p, c, f, j, e, ca).
  <Name>                                     The type name, e.g. Product or Dashboard.
  [<field:type> ...]                         Fields for a feature, e.g. Name:string Price:decimal.

Options:
  -o, --output <dir>         Directory to write into (default: derived from the artifact).
  -F, --feature <Name>       Co-locate under Features/<Name>/ instead of Features/Shared/ (component, job, email).
      --force                Overwrite existing files instead of refusing.
      --dry-run              Print what would be written without touching disk.

  Page options:
  -r, --route <path>         URL route for the page.

  Feature options (rask generate feature):
  -f, --fields <list>        Fields as Name:type,... (or pass them positionally).
  -c, --context <Name>       Reuse an existing DbContext instead of generating one.
  -p, --plural <Name>        Plural name for the feature folder/route (default: auto-pluralized).
      --id <guid|int|long>   Primary-key type (default: guid).
      --validation <mode>    Validation style: valueobjects (default), dataannotations, or fluent.
      --bs                   Render pages with Rask.Bootstrap (Bs*) components.
      --modal                Fold create/edit into a modal on the list page (implies --bs).
      --soft-delete          Soft-delete rows and add a Restore command.
      --concurrency          Add optimistic-concurrency (row version) handling.
      --events               Raise domain events on create/update/delete.
      --outbox               Persist domain events via the transactional outbox (implies --events).
      --tests                Generate a sibling <Project>.Tests project with domain + persistence tests.
      --no-restore           Write files wit

result.stdout:
Manage EF Core migrations (add, remove, list, update, drop).

Usage: rask db <add|remove|list|update|drop> [<name>] [--project <path>] [--startup-project <path>] [--context <Name>] [--output <dir>] [--force] [-- <ef args>]

Arguments:
  <add|remove|list|update|drop>   The migration action to run.
  [<name>]                        Migration name — required for 'add', e.g. InitialCreate.

Options:
  -p, --project <path>           Project containing the DbContext (default: found from the current directory).
  -s, --startup-project <path>   Startup project (default: same as --project).
  -c, --context <Name>           DbContext to use when the project defines more than one.
  -o, --output <dir>             Directory for the migration files (add only).
  -f, --force                    Skip the confirmation prompt (drop only).

Examples:
  rask db add InitialCreate
  rask db update
  rask db list
  rask db drop --force

result.stdout:
Build and deploy the app to a single host over SSH (auto-HTTPS with --domain).

Usage: rask deploy [status|logs|rollback] [--host user@box] [--domain app.example.com] [--port <n>] [--container-port <n>] [--project <path>] [--name <slug>] [--dockerfile <path>] [--env KEY=VALUE ...] [--env-file <path>] [--health-path <path>] [--no-health-check] [--setup-host] [--github-actions] [--dry-run]

Arguments:
  [status|logs|rollback]   Operate on what's already deployed instead of deploying (omit to deploy).

Options:
  -h, --host <user@box>      SSH target to build and run on (remembered in .rask/deploy.json).
  -d, --domain <host>        Public domain to serve over HTTPS via Caddy (implies ports 80/443).
      --port <n>             Published port when not using --domain (default: 8080).
      --container-port <n>   Port the app listens on inside the container (default: 8080; remembered).
  -p, --project <path>       Project to deploy (default: found from the current directory).
  -n, --name <slug>          Container/app name (default: derived from the project).
      --dockerfile <path>    Dockerfile to build (default: ./Dockerfile).
      --env-file <path>      File of KEY=VALUE lines to pass to the container.
  -e, --env <KEY=VALUE>      Environment variable to pass (repeatable).
      --health-path <path>   HTTP path probed for readiness before the blue-green swap (default: /health).
      --no-health-check      Skip the post-deploy HTTP health check.
      --github-actions       Write a .github/workflows/deploy.yml that runs this deploy on push, and print the secrets to add.
      --dry-run              Print the docker commands that would run without changing anything.
      --tail <n>             Log lines to show (logs only; default: 100, 'all' for everything).
  -f, --follow               Stream new log lines until interrupted (logs only).

  Host setup options (first deploy to a box):
      --setup-host           Prepare the host without asking (installs Docker, creates the deploy user, firewall, SSH hardening)
[truncated]
